claims.text: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type thin films and nanoribbons possess inherent native oxidation.
The as-deposited material has oxidation-associated compositional inhomogeneities.
Native oxidation induces localized lattice distortions near surfaces and interfaces.
Oxidation-induced lattice distortions enhance magnetic-domain pinning.
Oxidation-induced lattice distortions enhance magnetic frustration.
Native oxidation and its associated distortions govern the suppressed reversible magnetocaloric response during low-field cooling cycles.
Native oxidation and its associated distortions govern broadened magnetic hysteresis during low-field cooling cycles.
The low-dimensional films and nanoribbons behave differently from bulk forms.
A 300 degrees Celsius, 30-minute anneal in 5% H2 in N2 will reduce native oxidation.
The proposed reducing anneal will not induce significant grain growth or alter the overall microstructural design.
Surface oxidation creates local lattice strain and compositional gradients.
Local lattice strain and compositional gradients pin magnetic domain walls.
Domain-wall pinning stabilizes non-equilibrium magnetic configurations during low-field cycling.
Stabilization of non-equilibrium magnetic configurations broadens hysteresis.
Stabilization of non-equilibrium magnetic configurations reduces the reversible magnetocaloric effect.
Reducing the oxide content will relieve local lattice distortions.
The reducing anneal will produce a narrower hysteresis loop than the as-deposited baseline.
The reducing anneal will increase reversible isothermal entropy change and adiabatic temperature change relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The hypothesis applies at fields below 100 mT near the magnetic transition and for films thinner than 100 nm or nanoribbons narrower than 500 nm.
Heat-transfer limitations at higher cycling frequencies may influence the measured outcomes.
